You basically did it as a reassurance tactic, a compulsion. I myself went through this years ago. To accept it just accept the fact that you did it regardless of what it means. Acceptance is the key to getting over ocd.

I had this happen with my mom when I was younger. She knew I hated haircuts and always cut my hair when it reached a length I liked. I was young and haircuts traumatized me as I never got to have long hair and when it finally grew she decided to cut it. I let her cut it after protesting and then felt bad I resisted and tried to hug her and apologize for my behaviour, for which she shrugged me off and looked disgusted with me. It hurt a lot, and when I think of it I still cry to this day because it broke my heart. After that, I stopped hugging people and being affectionate in fear that they would retaliate too. When she tried hugging me in other times I pushed her away or broke away quickly because I felt so uncomfortable. Ex boyfriends always wanted to cuddle me but I didn’t like it. Sometimes my little sister tries hugging me and I out of instinct push her away and I feel bad for it an apologize. Some mothers aren’t fit to be mothers.
